newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban to reopen road to opposition-held north.
newsitem.headline: Taleban to reopen road to opposition-held north.

text.p: A senior Taleban official said on Thursday that they would reopen the road across the frontline to opposition-held areas in the north of the country for pedestrian traffic.

"It has been decided by the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Interior that the Salang Highway should be temporarily reopened," Amir Khan Mutaqi, the acting Minister of Information in the Taleban administration, told journalists.

The Salang highway is the main road between Kabul and the north of the country, which is in opposition hands. Some 120 km (75 miles) north of Kabul, it crosses the 3,600 metre-high (11,100 foot) Salang Pass, which marks the frontline between the Taleban and the opposition alliance.
When the Taleban advanced to the foot of the pass in January, the retreating opposition forces destroyed a bridge, closing the road to motor traffic.
The road was closed to pedestrian traffic early in March.
Mutaqi said the Taleban were reopening the road to ease the plight of refugees who had been trapped in Kabul by the closure.

"We have many people from the north who have been stranded south of the pass without shelter during the cold and wet weather. We are reopening the road temporarily, but we request people not to use unless it is absolutely necessary until we have defeated the rest of our enemies," said Mutaqi.
A report released by a Pakistan-based news agency on Thursday said that a large number of people had died from cold and in avalanches while trying to cross the mountains using alternative routes.

"On March 19, due to bad weather, heavy snowfall and avalanches, 190 people were killed in the Salang Pass. They were mostly travellers between the north and the south," said the report from the Afghan Islamic Press.
A foreign-based aid agency working in the area told Reuters that their workers had seen several bodies beside the road, but were unable to confirm the number of dead.

In Thursday's interview, Mutaqi also denied reports carried on Iranian radio the previous night that Qala-e-Naw, the capital of Badghis province in the northeast of the country, had fallen to opposition forces.
"There was heavy fighting on the frontline on the border between Badghis and Faryab provinces, but there has been no substantial change in positions. Nothing has happened in Qala-e-Naw," said Mutaqi.
There have been no independent witnesses to the fighting in the northeast.
